concepts.label: OnUpdate() handler
concepts.reused_or_minted: reused - promoted - used here purely as the contrast point for the omitsMutationBody finding below

relations.subject: eventing:on-delete-handler
relations.evidence: Note since the document is not available during an OnDelete we will filter by KEY prefix starting with "my\_data\_to\_flatten:".

notable_absence.finding: Beyond the omitsMutationBody fact above, this is a generic recursive document-flattening utility (nested objects/arrays -> underscore-joined flat keys) writing to a separate destination collection, with a matching OnDelete to keep the two in sync. Generic JS/data-transform technique in the standard handler boilerplate - no further Eventing mechanism to mint. Content is byte-identical to the Capella twin apart from front matter; the Capella twin's record left concepts/relations fully empty for this page even though the twin's page carries the identical 'document not available during OnDelete' sentence - this record captures that fact via the already-promoted omitsMutationBody predicate instead, since it fits the predicate's documented purpose exactly.

cross_product_finding: The destination collection this handler writes to is described as a hand-off point to other Couchbase/cloud infrastructure outside Eventing itself: "The destination collection can be shared (or replicated via XCDR to a business partner - maybe to AWS, GCP, or Azure)." This names XCDR and third-party cloud providers (AWS, GCP, Azure) as downstream consumers of Eventing output, but doesn't describe any Eventing-specific mechanism for that hand-off - a suggested pattern, not a documented feature. Identical wording recurs on the Capella twin and on the sibling genericRename/redactSharedData/simpleFlatten pages in this same batch.
